newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH RAIL STRIKE SHOWS NO SIGNS OF ENDING SOON.
newsitem.headline: CZECH RAIL STRIKE SHOWS NO SIGNS OF ENDING SOON.

text.p: Czech trains remained locked in railyards on Tuesday as a nationwide strike of railway workers showed no signs of ending soon.
From midnight, domestic and international passengers were stranded throughout the country, many on freezing platforms. Extra buses were called in to help carry local residents to work in many cities.

Czech transport minister Martin Riman on Tuesday said that the written demands of the unions, who are asking for a long-term reform plan for the debt-ridden railroads which protects jobs, were "anti-reform".
The Czech news agency CTK quoted him as saying that the strike had "schizophrenic" aims.
"It will be very difficult to agree on a version on which both sides would agree," it quoted Riman as saying about the possibility of a settlement.
The entire railway network came to a halt on Tuesday morning as the unions called the 48-hour strike demanding a complete overhaul of the decrepit rail system.

The Association of Unions of Rail Workers (OSZ), has threatended to prolong the stoppage if it does not get sufficient guarantees that acceptable long-term changes would be made in the railway system and its management.
Reports varied on how many of the more than 100,000 workers employeed by the state railways Ceske Drahy n.p. and its subsidiaries participated in the stike.

Leaders of the OSZ said that 75 to 80 percent of railway workers had joined the strike, but management of the railway company told CTK that over 60 percent showed up for work and signed a petition against the strike.
The railway workers' action comes at a time of mounting labour tensions in the public sector.
Last week, teachers began a rotating strike in selected schools, and there is simmering discontent in the health sector which led to sporadic industrial action last year.
